observations.excerpt:
## Decode allocation policy

By default, decode reserves each request's destination KV slots before prefill
finishes. Long prefills can hold these slots while decode waits for the KV data.
To delay this reservation, set the following flag on **both prefill and decode**:

```bash
--disaggregation-decode-allocation-policy prefill_complete
```

With `prefill_complete`, prefill computes without waiting for destination slots,
then signals readiness after accepting its final prefill result. Decode reserves
slots and starts the existing KV transfer handshake only after that signal.
This changes per-request KV reservation, not the size or creation of the global
KV pool. The default `early` policy preserves the existing behavior.

Deferring allocation can help when long prefills compete with active decode
requests for destination KV capacity. It also retains KV on prefill longer and
removes overlap between chunked prefill and KV transfer. Compare both policies
for your workload; this option is not a general throughput improvement.

This initial implementation requires Mooncake (RDMA or `mooncake_tcp`), the Python
bootstrap registry, and attention TP/CP and pipeline sizes of one. Attention DP
is allowed when each DP rank has attention TP size one. Prefill automatically
resolves `--optimistic-prefill-attempts` from zero to one; configurations that
disable optimistic prefill after model validation are rejected.
Chunked prefill does not yield just because decode has not admitted the request.
Completed requests retain their KV in the existing optimistic-prefill inflight
queue until decode supplies destination indices; readiness alone never starts
a KV write.
After a successful transfer, prefill clears the room's readiness and transfer
state before notifying decode of success. Retraction recovery can then reuse
the same bootstrap room. This notification waits for worker and scheduler
cleanup; failure and cancellation records remain until their timeout expires.
Retries remain eligible for prefill after the optimistic attempt budget is
exhausted and remain subject to the existing cancellation and timeout handling.

On prefill, `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT` starts after the final
prefill result, giving decode admission its own budget. On decode,
`SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_WAITING_TIMEOUT` bounds the wait for prefill completion,
then starts afresh for admission and again when destination indices are sent
for transfer.

The option does not support staging buffers, runtime PD role switching, PD
multiplexing, encoder disaggregation, decoupled speculation, HiSparse, decode radix cache, decode
HiCache, or non-DSA auxiliary state pools. Prefill HiCache is limited to L2 with
`write_back` and no storage backend. Unsupported configurations fail validation.

All communicating workers must use the same revision and enable the same policy. This
version of the decode worker rejects policy or peer-layout mismatches before
destination registration. Older decode workers do not enforce this check. Keep
`early` on both sides until every worker has been upgraded, then enable the new
policy on both sides.
observations.interpretation: Deferred reservation retains KV on prefill longer and removes prefill/transfer overlap. The document also records backend/layout constraints and the requirement to keep policies/revisions aligned across peers.

observations.excerpt:
### Prefill/Decode Disaggregation (PD)
- **Rust binary**
  ```bash
  ./target/release/sgl-model-gateway \
    --pd-disaggregation \
    --prefill http://prefill1:30001 9001 \
    --prefill http://prefill2:30002 \
    --decode http://decode1:30011 \
    --decode http://decode2:30012 \
    --policy cache_aware \
    --prefill-policy cache_aware \
    --decode-policy power_of_two
observations.interpretation: The gateway supports separate prefill and decode routing policies. This example is not evidence of a supported live policy setter.

observations.excerpt:
## Load Balancing Policies
- `random`: uniform random worker selection.
- `round_robin`: sequential rotation with atomic counters.
- `cache_aware`: maintains a prefix tree of prompts to route repeat traffic and evens load with configurable thresholds (`--cache-threshold`, `--balance-abs-threshold`, `--balance-rel-threshold`, `--eviction-interval`, `--max-tree-size`).
- `power_of_two`: chooses the lighter worker among two random candidates; integrates with `LoadMonitor`.
  Per-model overrides are available in PD mode (`--prefill-policy`, `--decode-policy`) and IGW mode via the worker registry.
observations.interpretation: Cache-aware routing has cache/load thresholds; power_of_two uses observed worker load. The cache-aware tree is router metadata, not the engine KV eviction policy.
Native runtime role switching requires an idle instance; rebuild failure is fatal and has no in-place rollback.
The role-switch handler rejects active work and checks headroom before a first decode graph capture. It does not migrate in-flight requests.
A switch rebuilds role-specific structures; rebuild failure marks the instance unhealthy. Decode graphs are prepared when required.

interpretation_limits: A field, consumer, or startup example does not establish a supported live setter.
Proposed request routing weights, admission caps, byte-credit backpressure, transfer fairness, and policy-version receipts remain research extensions.
Transport thread pools, request-slot capacity, backend/device selection, KV layout/dtype, TP/PP, and P:D role allocation are not first-version fine-grained live controls.
The native role switch drains the target instance; it does not satisfy the proposal's same-instance in-flight preservation contract.
Configuration combinations are constrained; deferred decode reservation, decode radix caching, and role switching must not be treated as independent simultaneously enabled knobs.
No new vLLM connector source audit was performed. SGLang PD controls must not be advertised as equivalent vLLM APIs.
No performance improvement or preferred P:D ratio has been measured.
